record.context_brief: Powers third and fourth eigenvalue problem
record.original_question: If G is a graph of order n, must the third and fourth largest adjacency eigenvalues satisfy lambda_i(G) <= floor(n/i) for i = 3 and i = 4?

evidence.quote: Problem 10 (Powers [129]). Let G be a graph of order n. Is it true that λ_i(G) ≤ floor(n/i) for i = 3, 4 ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a simple graph of order $n$, and let $A(G)$ denote its adjacency matrix. Order the eigenvalues of $A(G)$ as $\lambda_1(G) \ge \lambda_2(G) \ge \cdots \ge \lambda_n(G)$. Determine whether the following inequalities hold for every simple graph $G$ of order $n$:
$$\lambda_3(G) \le \left\lfloor \tfrac{n}{3} \right\rfloor \quad \text{and} \quad \lambda_4(G) \le \left\lfloor \tfrac{n}{4} \right\rfloor.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The case i=3 (whether λ₃(G) ≤ n/3) remains open in general, with partial affirmative results known for strongly regular graphs, regular line graphs, and Cayley/semi-Cayley graphs on abelian groups. The case i=4 has been disproved: Linz showed a construction with λ₄(G)/n ≥ (1+√5)/12 ≈ 0.2697 > 1/4, so the bound λ₄(G) ≤ n/4 fails.

status_evidence.title: On graphs with large third eigenvalue
status_evidence.snippet: evidence for c₃ = 1/3 ... partial affirmative response ... Linz's result showing c₄ ≥ (1+√5)/12 ≈ 0.26967 > 1/4
status_evidence.claim: λ₃ ≤ n/3 is open with partial results; λ₄ ≤ n/4 has been disproved.

status_evidence.title: On the third largest eigenvalue of graphs

status_evidence.claim: Active research line on bounding the third largest eigenvalue.
